key_insight: Wake interactions redistribute power between tandem rotors, while the highest system power coefficient occurs at L/D = 0.20, with the high-power Pareto region near λ = 10.
engineering_relevance: Surrogate-based optimization can help select rotor spacing and operating conditions that balance combined power capture against thrust on a shared support.
method: Simulate 160 tandem-rotor configurations under turbulent inflow using a vortex method.
Train per-time-node XGBoost models for 600 s load histories and extend them with a CNN-Attention-LSTM network.
Use a genetic algorithm to balance system power and thrust coefficients.
evidence_signal: Ten-fold cross-validation on unseen configurations yields median power-history R² values of 0.995 upstream and 0.958 downstream.
watch_item: The first-stage surrogate cannot extrapolate in tip-speed ratio, and the coefficients apply only below rated wind speed where both fixed-pitch rotors attain the simulated tip-speed ratio.
paper_title: Surrogate-Based Optimization of Tandem Twin-Rotor Wind Turbines Accounting for Wake Interactions
